static_traits.name: Wang Xinyi
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive friends and family; cooking and sharing are important parts of interpersonal interaction, but affected by negative beliefs
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar problem history; has not yet received prior counseling or treatment
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, can describe experiences concretely; highly cooperative; slightly Anxiety; able to discuss and accept the counseling plan

basic_info.main_problem: 'I have always believed the ethnic dishes I make taste terrible, although I really like cooking. This belief leaves me lacking motivation and affects my enjoyment of cooking.'
basic_info.core_demands: 'The persistent negative beliefs have affected my passion for cooking and my overall well-being, so I sought counseling.'
growth_experiences: A few months ago, a friend made a negative comment about a dish Wang Xinyi cooked; the comment has lingered in her mind ever since, gradually developing into the persistent belief that 'my cooking is terrible'. Although family often gives positive feedback (e.g., enthusiastic praise for a new dish last week), she still does not believe positive evaluations, thinking others are 'just being polite'. To improve, she took online courses and tried different recipes, but the negative belief persists, and her passion and enjoyment for cooking have markedly declined.

core_beliefs: My cooking is terrible; others will never truly like it
Negative evaluations are more real and credible than positive feedback

special_situations.event: A few months ago a friend gave a negative comment about one of her dishes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If someone criticizes, it means my cooking is always terrible / I have no cooking talent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replays negative evaluations and uses them as the standard of judgment, ignoring other positive evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He is telling the truth; this proves my cooking really is terrible.

special_situations.event: Family or friends praise the dish after tasting the food she made
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others praise, it is mostly out of politeness and does not reflect real skill
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittling the value of positive feedback, constantly seeking flaws to sustain the 'food is terrible' belief
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just being polite; actually the taste is not good.

special_situations.event: Every time before starting or during cooking ethnic dishes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If this dish does not meet my perfect standard, it equals failure / is inedible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeated checking, second-guessing, over-studying techniques to try to avoid failure feelings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time it will turn out awful again.

special_situations.event: When reviewing a cooking experience, both positive and negative feedback existed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative information is more credible and more representative of true level
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on negative evaluations; filters out positive evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That negative comment is the fact; other praise does not count.

core_conflict.wish: Longs for her effort and cooking to be truly seen and affirmed, gaining recognition as a 'liked and capable cook'
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated, laughed at, or seen as incompetent, causing shame and frustration
defense_goal: Prevents potential shame and hurt by belittling positive feedback and internalizing criticism
Controlling uncertainty and Anxiety by pursuing perfection and rationalized Learning

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a cook/self who could fail at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Picky and judgmental others (their affirmation is not credible)

behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing the other person is not sincere, just being polite (transference / Projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone peaceful and restrained, implicitly questions others' motives (such as 'you are just being polite'), avoiding directly accepting praise.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When uncertainty and Anxiety arise while preparing to cook or during cooking
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning emotional worries into technical problems, believing that as long as one learns more one can avoid failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use calm, technical language to talk about recipes and techniques, avoiding expressing subjective feelings (such as not directly talking about 'fearing it tastes bad').

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When recalling friends' negative comments about the dishes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizes the other's criticism as a stable self-evaluation standard
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Firm in tone, cites critical statements as 'factual basis' to veto other positive evidence.

manifestations: Once-loved cooking has become joyless and lifeless due to persistent Self-denial
Unable to internalize others' positive feedback as self-recognition, feeling dominated by external evaluations
outcomes: Increased anxiety and self-doubt, reduced sense of engagement and satisfaction in cooking

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizes a friend's one negative comment as a constant evaluation standard, believing 'criticism is more real'.

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'.
manifestations: When others praise, thinking 'they are just being polite', attributing one's own unease and doubt to the other person's motives.

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent Self-doubt and second-guessing while cooking, struggling to allow imperfection or accept positive feedback.

positive_force: Stable love for and dedication to cooking
Has a supportive network of family and friends
Able to proactively take action to Learning (taking online courses, trying different recipes)
negative_force: Overgeneralization, mental filtering, and negating-the-positive cognitive patterns reinforced Negative self-evaluation
Excessively depending on external evaluation (viewing criticism as more real), difficult to internalize positive feedback
Anxiety and Self-doubt frequently triggered in cooking situations, leading to Decreased drive

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent Self-denial and Anxiety when cooking ethnic dishes (insisting 'it tastes terrible' and negating others' praise)
antecedent: Starting to prepare or cook ethnic dishes
When family / friends give positive feedback
target_behavior.core_reason: Generalizes a single negative evaluation into a stable conclusion, filters positive information, and overly relies on external evaluation to assess their own ability
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the shame and Anxiety of 'being exposed' short-term by negating positive feedback, gaining a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced cooking enjoyment and engagement, Decreased drive; interaction quality with family and friends affected (struggling to accept praise)
